channel.title: The Seax: Essex news, sport and life
channel.description: The latest Essex news, sport and life, updated through the day.

image.title: The Seax: Essex news, sport and life

item.title: Anglia Ruskin study finds most dog attacks are preventable
item.description: Owners losing control of their dogs is the biggest single cause of bites, university research for Battersea finds. Many breeds are involved.

item.title: Forensic scientist Sue Black formally invested as ARU chancellor at Chelmsford Cathedral
item.description: One of the world's leading forensic scientists, named Anglia Ruskin University's chancellor in September, has been formally invested at its Chelmsford graduations.

item.title: Benfleet twin sisters to work as midwives at Basildon Hospital
item.description: Ella and Freya Ward, 21, graduated together in Chelmsford. Both trained on placement at Basildon Hospital and will now work there.

item.title: Missing Harlow man found, police say
item.description: Essex Police has ended its appeal for a 45-year-old man reported missing from Harlow on Friday.

item.title: Harlow driver banned for 40 months after drink-driving with child in front
item.description: A Harlow woman has lost her licence for drink-driving. A toddler was sitting unrestrained in her front passenger seat.

item.title: Basildon town centre safety wardens and underpass clean-up get go-ahead
item.description: Wardens would patrol five days a week from early 2027, alongside brighter lighting and deep-cleaned underpasses.

item.title: Stacey Solomon and Joe Swash film Christmas show on Epping Ongar Railway
item.description: The couple rode the heritage line's festive light train for their BBC One series. The railway says their visit added extra sparkle.

item.title: Basildon Borough Volunteer Awards open for nominations
item.description: Nominations close at 11.59pm on Friday 18 December. Winners will be named at the Towngate Theatre in March.

item.title: Brentwood Council must pay Cala's costs after losing Priests Lane appeal
item.description: An inspector allowed 97 homes on a former school playing field near Shenfield, overturning a refusal made against planning officers' advice.

item.title: KFC applies to serve hot food until 3am on Brentwood High Street
item.description: Residents have until 18 December to comment on the plan, which would run to 3am from Thursday to Saturday.

item.title: Wickford man jailed over £30m cocaine pick-up from the sea
item.description: Cameron Weedon helped fishermen fetch 374kg of cocaine dumped in the Channel. A gang leader from Rainham was also jailed.

item.title: Braintree Town FC mascot Buddy the Boar leads town centre Christmas trail
item.description: The council and the football club's mascot have set up a Christmas trail. It runs around Braintree town centre.

item.title: Clacton Leisure Centre hosts free NHS health checks on Monday
item.description: Clacton residents can get blood pressure checks and flu jabs at a free NHS event. Researchers will also show studies people can join.

item.title: Grays prison tutor spared jail over secret relationship with inmate
item.description: Oksana Antanaitiene, 52, a maths tutor at HMP Chelmsford, used a false name and a secret phone to keep in touch with him.

item.title: c2c trains delayed across network after fire near Grays line
item.description: A fire beside the railway at Grays slowed c2c trains on every route. Delays were expected until about 6pm.

item.title: Work starts on stalled Braintree link road to Panfield Lane
item.description: Building has begun on a road linking Springwood Drive and Panfield Lane. It had stalled for years while developers argued over timing.

item.title: Southend boss Dyer calls Hartlepool's 5.30pm kick-off a 'shambles'
item.description: Southend United fans face another late start at the far end of the country. The manager says they will still travel in their hundreds.

item.title: Buses replace trains across south Essex this weekend
item.description: Rail passengers from Shenfield, Southend and the Crouch Valley face replacement buses on Saturday and Sunday. Dartford Crossing works are paused for Black Friday.

item.title: Epping Forest District Council backs plan to prevent homelessness
item.description: A new five-year plan aims to stop people in the Epping Forest district losing their homes. Requests for help are up a quarter since 2022.

item.title: Beat the Street players in eastern Thurrock walk 35,201 miles
item.description: Schools and teams from Stanford-le-Hope, Corringham and nearby villages were honoured after the six-week walking game.

item.title: Grays Christmas tree lights switched on by Mayor of Thurrock
item.description: Families packed Grays High Street for the town's annual switch-on and Christmas fair.

item.title: Essex patients missed almost 37,000 GP surgery appointments in September
item.description: It is the highest monthly figure this year. NHS Essex is asking patients to cancel appointments they cannot make.

item.title: Ingatestone Festive Fair brings 30 stalls to the High Street on Sunday
item.description: Brentwood's Christmas lights are now on. The borough's free festive events move on to Ingatestone and Shenfield.

item.title: Greater Anglia shuts Shenfield to London line for 8 days after Christmas
item.description: Essex rail passengers face buses to the Tube for a week over New Year. Trains also finish early on Christmas Eve.

item.title: One in three Essex takeaways misses top food hygiene rating
item.description: The Seax checked every food hygiene rating in Essex. Takeaways fare worst, and Tendring's lag the rest of the county.

item.title: Lakeside's Slim Chickens restaurant opens on 10 December
item.description: The US chicken chain is bringing 50 jobs to the Thurrock shopping centre. Its first 5,000 customers each get a prize card.

item.title: Brentwood man charged with rape at Soho's Groucho Club
item.description: Stefan-Pierre Tomlin, 36, is due at Southwark Crown Court on Monday. He also faces two counts of assault by penetration.

item.title: Maldon High Street arson: police appeal for information
item.description: Two people tried to break into a High Street business and start a fire at about 2.30am. Salt Bar Pizza Grill says it is open as usual.

item.title: Braintree Recycling Centre opens free 'Santa's Grotto' for Christmas reuse
item.description: Unwanted Christmas trees and decorations left at the Braintree tip are now free to take home.

item.title: Havens Hospices cyclists ride 500km from Devon to Southend
item.description: A father and son rode from Devon to Fair Havens hospice in Southend. They raised more than £4,000 for the hospice that cared for family.

item.title: Essex urgent treatment centres under review
item.description: NHS Essex wants to hear where people go when they need help fast. Its survey will shape a new plan for urgent care.

item.title: Harlow man, 41, sent to crown court on strangulation charge
item.description: A Harlow man has been charged over an alleged offence in the town on 7 November. He is on bail until a crown court hearing.

item.title: Witham special school rated strong in every area by Ofsted
item.description: Southview School got the second-highest grade in all eight areas. Four other Essex primaries also had new report cards published this week.

item.title: Southend names Nigel Folkard Honorary Alderman
item.description: Southend's councillors also gave certificates to a dance school, a powerlifter and the Masonic centre at Saxon Hall.

item.title: Essex gets £1.1m to tackle stalking
item.description: Stalkers across Essex will be offered help to change their behaviour. Victims get more specialist support, including help with online tracking.

item.title: Stansted Airport Poppy Appeal raises record £26,190
item.description: Passengers and staff at Stansted gave more than ever to this year's Poppy Appeal. The total beat last year's record by over £2,000.

item.title: Shoeburyness East Beach could get dunes and step-free boardwalk
item.description: Southend City Council plans to replace worn sea defences at East Beach with replanted dunes. Work could start in spring 2027.

item.title: Southend crash: police seek dashcam footage after man seriously hurt
item.description: A pedestrian in his 40s was hit by a car in Sutton Road last Saturday. Police want witnesses and footage.

item.title: Harwich Town Council plans to digitise its Guildhall archive
item.description: Harwich's Guildhall holds thousands of historic papers, some from the late 1200s. The town council wants to start putting them online.

item.title: Lakeside gets bigger Superdry and new perfume shop before Christmas
item.description: West Thurrock's Lakeside Shopping Centre is adding shops and festive events. Superdry has moved to a larger unit opposite Boots.

item.title: Southend Sea Life Adventure wins appeal to keep wider entrance canopy
item.description: A planning inspector has overruled Southend councillors over the seafront attraction's canopy. They said it narrowed the pavement for disabled people.

item.title: Thurrock Council says sorry over Grays Town Park cafe rent demand
item.description: A Reform councillor says the demand was sent without authorisation. The council will meet the volunteers to agree a way forward.

item.title: Essex's Prodigy star Keith Flint honoured with fossil snail name
item.description: Scientists have named a 99-million-year-old snail after the late Prodigy singer. Its hairy shell reminded them of his famous spiky hair.

item.title: Basildon end-terrace house destroyed by fire as crews protect neighbours
item.description: An end-terrace house in Basildon was completely alight when firefighters arrived. Smoke spread to the home next door.

item.title: Southend United legend Frankie Banks given Freedom of the City
item.description: The former Shrimpers full-back started the club's community work in 1991. The club says his impact goes far beyond the pitch.

item.title: Harlow Council tells government to drop asylum plan for private homes
item.description: The Home Office's contractor wants to rent homes across Harlow for asylum seekers. The council's leader wants the plan dropped.

item.title: Chelmsford murder trial: boy, 17, tells jury he carried knife for protection
item.description: A teenager accused of murdering Radwan Shakur in Central Park has given evidence. He denies being part of any turf war.

item.title: Weeley and Little Clacton bypasses to shut for four nights from 7 December
item.description: Drivers heading to and from Clacton face overnight closures on two bypasses. The road is being resurfaced.

item.title: Saffron Walden Museum catalogue goes online with 60,000 records
item.description: Anyone can now browse the town museum's collection records from home, the Saffron Walden Reporter reported.

item.title: Colchester man admits 10 thefts from garage he was banned from
item.description: Danny Archer, 40, took £550 of meat and other food from the BP in Ipswich Road. He has been remanded in custody.

item.title: Navestock fly-tippers targeted by Brentwood police van checks
item.description: Police and council officers are patrolling Brentwood's country lanes and stopping vans. The borough sees about three fly-tips a day.

item.title: Leigh police stop finds £1m of cocaine as driver is jailed
item.description: Officers found 8kg in a car boot, then 7kg more in a Southend storage unit. Douglas Kramer got six years and eight months.

item.title: Essex farmers raise fly-tipping costs at first county roundtable
item.description: Farmers told Essex County Council that rural crime and the cost of clearing dumped waste hurt them. More meetings are planned.

item.title: c2c gets £2m plan to fix delays
item.description: Rail bosses are spending more to fix the Southend line after months of delays. Some December trains will finish early or be replaced by buses.

item.title: Thurrock Council says no decision yet on selling 70 acres of open space
item.description: Three sites in Linford, Tilbury and Corringham could be sold. Residents have until 27 November to object, and cabinet would have the final say.

item.title: Essex GP surgeries to offer 32,000 extra appointments this winter
item.description: NHS Essex is paying for 8,000 more GP appointments a month until February. It is part of a county-wide plan for the busiest season.

item.title: Chelmsford parents back Havens Hospices appeal after baby son's care
item.description: Michael and Sarah Fragnito's son Elio spent his last two days at the Little Havens children's hospice. They now support its Christmas appeal.

item.title: Thurrock CVS invites would-be volunteers to drop in after Tilbury winter event
item.description: Thurrock CVS says anyone curious about volunteering can get in touch. Its co-ordinator met many residents at a busy Tilbury winter event.

item.title: Rayleigh shoplifter jailed for five months after BP garage thefts
item.description: Stefan Jaworski, 44, stole £260 of meat, fish, chocolate and alcohol. A court order bans him from every BP in England and Wales.

item.title: Southend signs 12-month contract for enviro-crime crackdown officers
item.description: Extra enforcement officers will target dog fouling and littering in Southend town centre.
